description: ⚚ The coding harness with Hermes Agent wired into IDE.
readmeExcerpt:
**All-in-one package for Hermes Agent. Install once, then just type `dag-ulw`.** [English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [Русский](README.ru.md) | [한국어](README.ko.md) | [Español](README.es.md) | [Français](README.fr.md) | [Deutsch](README.de.md) | [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md) | [Italiano](README.it.md) **oh-my-hermes** is an operating layer for [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent).
You keep talking to Hermes. OMH picks the skill and a model for each lane, and runs the work in parallel.
It never patches or replaces Hermes, and it never reports planned work as done.
## Install ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes/main/install.sh | sh omh setup ``` [Windows and other options →](docs/INSTALLATION.md)
## What you get - **The right model for every lane.**
Each lane is tagged with a work category: `ultrabrain`, `deep`, `visual-engineering`, `quick` and more.
The category picks that lane's model chain and reasoning effort, and you can edit every chain.
When a provider rejects a model, the chain moves to the next one instead of silently downgrading.
`omh model` opens the picker; [see which model runs each lane](docs/INSTALLATION.md#guided-model-setup). - **`/dag-ulw` graph runs.**
Your goal becomes a graph of small nodes, and the ready ones run in parallel.
Each node runs on its category's model and effort; nodes running at once never share a write scope.
A separate node checks the goal, and failed nodes are repaired before the report. - **Expert skills on demand.**
A hundred-plus `omh-*` specialists: frontend, backend, Rust, security review, verification gates.
You never call them; the router loads the right ones into the run as tool calls. - **LSP in the loop.**
Definitions, references and renames come from the language server, not text search.
Aliases, re-exports and shadowed names are renamed by meaning, not by matching text.
Off by default; enable `lsp_tools` in the OMH plugin settings. - **Long-term memory you can trust.**
Nothing is remembered silently: each candidate is kept, refused or deferred with a written reason.
The next session gets a recall pack ranked for its task and cut to a token budget.
Hermes' own memory is never read or patched. - **OMH Native.**
Bare `omh` opens OMH's own TUI on Hermes' gateway; switch its launch look with `/theme`.
`/dag-ulw` prints the box graph, then a live lane tree with each lane's model, effort and tokens.
Steer or interrupt an agent from the agent list, run a `!` shell line, and rewind with Esc Esc. - **Evidence before "done".**
Every status names its stage and how sure OMH is about it.
`Plan · not run` · `Code · reported done` · `Test · verified`
A run counts as verified only when a test, review or CI gate actually passed.
## DAG-ULW **Just type `/dag-ulw`, and you're a graph engineering master.** Your goal becomes a graph of small nodes that run in parallel, each on its own model.
A separate node verifies the goal before you get the report.

Reference

Ultra-Skills

Ten ulw- workflows. Say the trigger in chat — Hermes routes the rest. Full catalog: Workflow Reference.

Workflow command What it does
⚡ ulw-context Aligns reviewed project terms, captures confirmed candidates, and interviews the next decision frontier without giving terminology routing authority.
⚡ ulw-interview Asks one question at a time until it knows exactly what you want.
⚡ ulw-research Digs through real code and the live web, keeps sources, and verifies anything doubtful.
⚡ ulw-plan Builds a reviewed plan: options compared, risks named, done-criteria agreed.
⚡ ulw-work Runs an accepted plan in parallel lanes that never touch the same file.
⚡ dag-ulw Runs a big job as a graph of small parallel nodes, verifies the goal with a separate node, and repairs what failed.
⚡ ulw-maestro Runs a delegated task on Claude Code or Codex — prompt composed from the CLI's own installed skills, spawned live with a dock row and a steerable session.
⚡ ulw-loop Cycles plan → build → review until the goal actually passes.
⚡ ulw-qa Attacks the build with hostile scenarios and fixes what breaks.
⚡ ulw-perf Measures where it is actually slow or expensive, then fixes one hot path at a time.

Recommended set

Type these at the Hermes prompt. The ulw- prefix picks the workflow; the rest is your request in plain words.

1. Shape it. ulw-interview when the idea is still fuzzy, ulw-plan when the change is known but risky.

❯ ulw-interview: I want a CLI that tracks the ISS and warns me before it passes overhead
❯ ulw-plan: analyze this project's circular dependencies and plan the refactor

2. Build it. ulw-work runs the accepted plan in parallel lanes that never edit the same file.

❯ ulw-work: run the accepted plan

3. Finish it. ulw-loop keeps cycling until the gate you name passes.

❯ ulw-loop: keep going until npm test passes

How it works with Hermes

Hermes Agent already runs the loop. OMH decides what goes into it: which model and effort each lane gets, who owns the code change, which skills apply, and what counts as done. Two rules hold everywhere: model choice and coding ownership are separate decisions, and nothing prepared is ever reported as executed. The generated catalog, triggers, and evidence rules live in Workflow Reference.

The workflow

Understand → Research → Decide → Plan → Execute → Verify → Operate → Learn

Stage What happens
Understand Confirm the intent, constraints, project terms, and stop conditions.
Research Replace assumptions with source-backed product, code, or operational context.
Decide Make the options, tradeoffs, and decision owner explicit.
Plan Turn accepted scope, coding ownership, tests, and done criteria into an executable plan.
Execute Dispatch bounded work to the selected owner and track what actually runs; a prepared handoff is not execution evidence.
Verify Base the verdict on observed test results, review findings, CI status, and runtime evidence.
Operate Keep release health, incidents, rollback state, and follow-up work visible.
Learn Promote reviewed, scoped lessons into project memory or workflow improvements.

Highlights

Intelligence What OMH adds
🧭 Mixture-of-models routing Every delegated lane lands on a category (model + reasoning effort) at dispatch time. Chains fall through when a provider rejects a model, and a child that did no work shows failed, never a green row.
🎛️ Per-family calibration Prompting is tuned per model family and generation — GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6, Claude 5.5, GLM 5.3, Kimi, Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek and more — and each tune is kept only while the benchmark pair says it helps.
🗂️ Categories you own Shipped model categories, with omh model-chains set to reorder, an entitlement interview that reorders chains per machine, and a live view of what a request would route to before it runs.
🖥️ Native TUI surface The OMH HUD (live rows with category, turns, cost, cache), the phase todo above the prompt, parallel shot ×N, full-row diff bands, and a theme of your own — in the OMH TUI bare omh opens, never patching Hermes.
⚡ Observed parallel work Independent work splits into fanout units with disjoint file ownership, admission control under provider pressure, typed result sidecars, and verification gates that read what came back.
💸 Priced cost telemetry Token counts and dollar figures on every HUD row and run summary, priced from a rate table that cites its source; an unpriceable run reads unknown, never $0.
🧠 Long-term project memory A file-backed memory provider Hermes loads, admission and retention policies, reviewer-gated writes, and recall packs with freshness and budget — Hermes' own memory stays untouched.
🔎 Structural code search A measured ast-grep playbook (28 languages, grep fallback) and omh codegraph uml for a repo-wide architecture picture, injected where executors read code; omh codegraph tests --changed names the tests a change reaches (codegraph commands).
🛡️ Guardrails you write Toolcall rules that block an off-script call with your own rule text, a completion-integrity gate that refuses stubs and skipped tests as evidence, and an approval tier for risky actions.
♾️ Ultra workflow engines Parallel delivery lanes, measured goal loops with ledgers and real completion gates, and decision-frontier interviews before any engine runs — listed in Ultra-Skills above.
📦 A deterministic catalog A hundred-plus installable skills generated from one source, routing precision corpora with negative controls, and drift gates that fail CI on a single divergent byte.

Evidence before claims

OMH never reports that work happened unless it watched it happen. Every status you see has two parts: the stage, and how sure OMH is about it.

You see It means
Plan · not run A prompt or plan is ready. Nothing has run yet.
Code · running An executor is running now, and OMH is watching it.
Code · reported done The executor said it finished. Nobody checked the result.
Test · verified A test, review, or CI gate actually passed.

An executor saying it is done is not the same as anything having been checked, and most tools spell both "complete". Capability impact is reported across separate dimensions rather than one marketing score; see Capability Impact. The product A/B lane that compares Hermes alone with Hermes through OMH has its corpus and offline pilot in place, and no measured run is published yet: benchmarks/product-ab/v1/README.md.

- **In a console session a choice goes through Hermes' `clarify` picker, and
  the OMH TUI draws that picker the way Claude Code draws its question
  dialog.** On the first turn of an attended `cli`, `tui` or `desktop`
  session, the model is asked to use `clarify` where its reply would stop for
  the person to pick between named options or approve an action it will not
  take without their answer, instead of listing the options in prose and
  asking for a word back. A closing offer of optional further work stays
  prose. After a clarify timed out, the person's next message brings the same
  ask once more. Messaging platforms, single-query runs, kanban task
  processes and delegated children get nothing and render the same bytes as
  before. In the OMH TUI a question with choices now stands between two
  rules: the context dim, the question itself bold, a `label — description`
  choice as its label with the description under it, `Type something.` for
  an answer of your own, and the keys on a row of their own with how long the
  question has waited. The tool row says how many choices it offers instead
  of repeating the question. A pick still answers with Hermes' own choice

releases.name: v4.0.5
releases.body:
- **Matching a coding handoff to a specialist domain is about 2.7 times
  faster on English text.** Preparing a handoff folds the task message and the
  plan text before it matches specialist domains, and ran the full Unicode
  normalisation on every pass even for plain ASCII, which that work cannot
  change. ASCII text now takes a direct lowercase fold, and text that is still
  ASCII after the first normalisation step returns early. Other text keeps the
  original steps in the original order, so routing decisions, exclusions and
  errors are identical. On the domain-routing benchmark 772.81 ms fell to
  290.94 ms (median of three runs). Contributed by @dexhunter (#2536).

- **Memory recall shows what the turn asked for, once per conversation.**
  A message with nothing to search for (an empty turn, "야") used to get every
  saved memory in full; it now gets pinned ones in full and the rest as the
  one-line list of names a non-matching message already gets. A
  background-process or delegation notice that nobody typed gets nothing at
  all. A memory the conversation already holds is not sent again until it
  changes or a compaction drops it, and a list of names it was already shown

releases.name: v4.0.3
releases.body:
- **`plan` and `ralplan` name the goal beyond the request, the raw material,
  and an outside judge.** Before splitting tasks a plan states what should
  happen once the requested result exists and whether it aims there, and adds
  the access an executor needs to work at that level unattended as its own
  tasks; it starts from raw logs, traces or data rather than a digest, names
  the methods a leading practitioner would use, and gives every verification
  step a judge other than the planner or executor, recording a missing one as
  an evidence gap; it restates the deliverable as verbs and brings other
  fields in as practitioner actions, never as voices to imitate. The lines sit
  after each bar's first four items, so capability rows do not move, and they
  reach the portable projection.
- **3D and canvas scenes have a craft and QA bar.** A user ran the same voxel
  pagoda garden prompt through two agents: both consoles were clean, and the
  OMH build was judged less colorful. Its first frame was flat noon under its
  own "golden hour" subtitle, and its birds read as floating black cubes, and
  nothing in the catalog named a 3D scene, so neither the build nor its own
  visual revi

releases.name: v4.0.2 · Kami
releases.body:
# Oh My Hermes 4.0.2 — Kami

Kami makes dag-ulw the default for plain multi-part jobs, while it reads the
remarks after a request more strictly. It also rebuilds the OMH TUI launch and
transcript, keeps each conversation's delegation route its own, onboards Kimi
K3.1 Pro into every Kimi K3 slot, and adds new science, job-search and
show-reel skills.

## dag-ulw is the default for a job over many targets

A plain request for a change over many targets now runs as a dag-ulw graph,
with no `dag ulw` needed (`update every service to node 22`, `열린 PR들 전부
리베이스해줘`). The router starts one only on positive evidence: a change verb
from a closed allow list, on an object that names independent units, or two
named parts asked for in parallel. Work over many targets without that
evidence (`review all open PRs`) is at most offered, as one question. A
request that reads, reports, stops, holds, is conditional, is in the past, or
is scoped to one PR does not start a run. Measured on the frozen acceptance
sets; prompts outside them are not measured. (#2232) Hermes' route hint never
starts a dag-ulw run on a split the router would only ask about, and a split

aiSummary.oneLiner: An operating layer for Hermes Agent providing capabilities for planning, research, and project memory orchestration.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: oh-my-hermes acts as a robust operating layer sitting directly above the NousResearch Hermes Agent. It enhances the standard agent workflow by adding explicit capabilities for task planning, deep research, coding handoffs, and persistent project memory management. The framework evaluates raw requests to automatically select the most appropriate workflow and evidence gates before executing native skills. By maintaining an honest record of actions taken, it strengthens existing operational processes without hiding or replacing the underlying Hermes execution engine.
keyFeatures: Workflow orchestration: Automatically selects appropriate operational workflows based on the complexity of the agent request.
Persistent memory: Maintains project-level context and an explicit record of all actions taken by the agent.
Evidence gating: Establishes clear boundaries and verification steps before executing critical coding tasks.
Multilingual support: Provides comprehensive documentation and interfaces in English, Korean, Japanese, and Chinese.
Native skill execution: Runs Hermes skills directly without abstracting away the core execution layer.
